Q: Filtering time with CAST string AS TIMESTAMP fails A:

In IoTDB 2.0.8 table model, CAST('2025-07-01 00:00:00' AS TIMESTAMP) is not a usable form for a WHERE time ... range predicate. The parser accepts the syntax, but the planner path for the time filter expects a numeric timestamp literal, so the cast expression reaches it as a GenericLiteral and produces the GenericLiteral cannot be cast to ... LongLiteral error.

Use epoch-millisecond boundaries for the time predicate, as in your control query:

sql
SELECT time, meter_id, kwh
FROM meter_energy
WHERE time >= 1751299200000
  AND time <  1751385600000;

For the report generator, convert the UI day strings before building/binding the SQL predicate, and keep the half-open range form:

WHERE time >= <start_epoch_ms>
  AND time <  <end_epoch_ms>

A quoted string comparison is not an equivalent workaround here; it is a STRING expression, not a numeric TIMESTAMP boundary. Treat the class-cast exception as the current 2.0.8 failure mode for this unsupported predicate shape, rather than as evidence that the casted timestamp predicate is supported.

Q: Fatal Exception: Bad state: Too many elements A:

It is coming from your this call:

rwScrollController.position.pixels

.position in here uses .single in it. Before use, check it like that:

if (rwScrollController.positions.length != 1) return;

        Try
            Dim DataReturn As New DataSet
            command.CommandType = CommandType.Text
            command.Connection.Open()
            NumberitemInserted = command.ExecuteNonQuery()
            command.Connection.Close()
        Catch ex As Exception
            NumberitemInserted = -1
        Finally
            command.Connection.Close()
        End Try
        Return NumberitemInserted
    End Function
    Public Function SQL_ArrayList(ByVal Sqlcommand As String) As ArrayList
        connection = New SqlConnection(connectionString)

        Dim ArString As New ArrayList
        Try
            connection.Open()
            Dim command As SqlCommand = _
                   New SqlCommand(Sqlcommand, connection)
            command.CommandType = CommandType.Text
            Dim DR As SqlDataReader = command.ExecuteReader
            Do While DR.Read
                ArString.Add(DR.GetValue(0))
            Loop
        Catch ex As Exception
            MsgBox(ex.Message)
        Finally
            connection.Close()
        End Try
        Return ArString

    End Function
    Public Function getStringItem(ByVal Sqlcommand As String) As String
        connection = New SqlConnection(connectionString)
        Dim itemSTR As String = Nothing
        Try
            connection.Open()
            Dim command As SqlCommand = _
                   New SqlCommand(Sqlcommand, connection)
            command.CommandType = CommandType.Text
            Dim DR As SqlDataReader = command.ExecuteReader
            Do While DR.Read
                itemSTR = ObjectToString(DR.GetValue(0))
            Loop
        Catch ex As Exception
            itemSTR = ""
        Finally
            connection.Close()
        End Try
        Return itemSTR
    End Function
    Public Function ObjectToString(ByVal obj As Object) As String
        Try
            If IsDBNull(obj) Then
                Return ""
            ElseIf obj = Nothing Then
                Return ""
            Else
                Return obj
            End If
        Catch ex As Exception
            Return ""
        End Try
    End Function

End Module

Q: What are Wrappers in ReactJS? A:

<BrowserRouter> and <SomeContext.Provider> are React components, not special HTML tags.

They look like HTML because of JSX. JSX is just syntax sugar that gets compiled into JavaScript function calls.

For example:

<BrowserRouter>
  <App />
</BrowserRouter>

is transformed into something similar to:

React.createElement(
  BrowserRouter,
  null,
  React.createElement(App, null)
);

The content between the opening and closing tags becomes the component’s children prop.

So a wrapper component is simply a component that renders its children while adding some behavior. For example, BrowserRouter provides routing context, and SomeContext.Provider provides a context value to all descendant components.

There is nothing special about the opening and closing tags—they’re just JSX syntax representing a component with children.

Q: Open notebook menu not available in my Lakehouse A:

  1. Switch the View: Look at the top-right corner of the screen (just below the main Fabric header ribbon). Select Lakehouse instead of SQL analytics endpoint

  2. Select Lakehouse: Click that dropdown and switch it back to Lakehouse.

  3. Access the Notebook Menu: Once the UI switches back to the Lakehouse view, the ribbon across the top will update, and the Open notebook (or Notebook > New notebook) option will reappear in the ribbon.
